commit.subject: wip Vulkan support allocating resource table
commit.message:
wip Vulkan support allocating resource table

Bugs found with the test:

 - vulkan::ResourceTable didn't initialize ResourceTableBase which in
   turn didn't initialize the DynamicArrayState.
 - vulkan::DeviceVk didn't take into account the new feature in the
   logic around enabling/disabling robustness.
 - The descriptor set allocation in vulkan::ResourceTable didn't account
   for reserved entries for default resources.

Change-Id: I34fbf35874773c3199f5d829df4003a519bd54a2

commit.subject: dawn_json_generator.py: Sort objects so that optional object arguments come first
commit.message:
dawn_json_generator.py: Sort objects so that optional object arguments come first

For example, "render bundle encoder.set bind group" depends optionally
on "bind group", so we generate:

inline void SetBindGroup(..., BindGroup const& group = nullptr, ...) const;

Assigning `nullptr` to a `BindGroup const&` works because BindGroup has
an implicit constructor that accepts nullptr; however, this also means
that BindGroup must be fully defined before RenderBundle for the
compiler to compile this function.

So far we've been lucky, but my next CL hit this issue, so this fixes
it.

Bug: 463925499
Change-Id: I90b44757d45b288786ea9abe9126fc0bcca8d24a

commit.message:
[tint][val] Improve type validation for IO attributes

Adds in missing type testing for IO attributes, so that non-allowed types are
rejected, instead of silently getting through

Clean up of the BuiltinChecker for how it reports type errors

Added type error checking to IOAttributeChecker

Merges kAllowWorkspacePointerInputToEntryPoint, kAllowPrivateVarsInFunctions,
kAllowPointersAndHandlesInStructures into a single capability
kMslAllowEntryPointInterface

commit.subject: [ir] Fail gracefully for invalid internal immediate offsets
commit.message:
[ir] Fail gracefully for invalid internal immediate offsets

Instead of triggering an ICE, fail gracefully by returning a `Failure`
from the transform.

This fixes a WGSL fuzzer failure where the user-provided offsets were
causing overlaps.

Fixed: 466305312
Change-Id: Ife1c8a10a325d1e729d7762ca6abefba0f55f31d

commit.subject: [fuzz] Writer failure should not cause fuzzer failure
commit.message:
[fuzz] Writer failure should not cause fuzzer failure

The writers can fail gracefully on bad input (e.g. invalid
user-provided options), and this should not cause a fuzzer
failure. Capture these errors and return them through the `Result`
instead of triggering an ICE.

This will allow us to perform more validation of user-provided options
at the point of use instead of during `CanGenerate()`.

Bug: 467330780
Change-Id: Ica72a4b90af572b2819981e4938b250ec83ba435

commit.subject: [spirv] Always use constants for struct member access
commit.message:
[spirv] Always use constants for struct member access

We recently introduced a bitcast for access operands to avoid a
spirv-val check from firing on negative indices. This bitcast turns
some constants into non-constants, which is invalid for struct member
access in SPIR-V.

This would never be an issue when coming from WGSL because struct
member indices always become unsigned values, but the IR supports
signed indices too and so the fuzzers found this case.

Add an extra case for constants to make sure that they stay as
constants to fix this.

Fixed: 466695222
Change-Id: I160ad2f305e767e49142b218d1cf0a6f051db96c

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Use "slot" instead of "i" in DynamicArrayState
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Use "slot" instead of "i" in DynamicArrayState

The use of "i" could be confused with a loop index so use a different
name. In the future when DynamicArrayState is used only for
ResourceTable, it will use a new TypedInteger called ResourceTableSlot
so preemptively use the slot terminology.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: Ie3700d186fdcddee02e33782ec16ab61aca8a405

commit.message:
Fix webgpu_dawn exported symbols.

DEFINE_PREFIX = "WGPU"
didn't apply to sources in webgpu_dawn_native_proc_sources target,
thus they didn't compile
with WGPU_IMPLEMENTATION and WGPU_SHARED_LIBRARY defined,
so move these sources into webgpu_dawn target directly.

This also fixes MSVC component build,
which wasn't generating LIB file,
because the DLL didn't export any symbols.

commit.message:
Kotlin: Internalize and move getException to WebGpuRuntimeException companion

prevents the public API surface for exception creation by devs.

commit.subject: Vulkan, GL: no-op BytesPerSample attachment limit
commit.message:
Vulkan, GL: no-op BytesPerSample attachment limit

Only Metal has a limit on the total number of bytes per sample
in attachments. As D3D* do, give Vulkan and GL the maximum value so
this limit becomes a no-op.

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add end2end tests for Update/Insert/RemoveBinding

The tests found an issue where RemoveBinding didn't internally remove
the binding, which caused a subsequent call to Update to early-out, skip
updating the metadata buffer, and caused the resource to not be visible.

the `${install_prefix}/bin` directory when using `cmake
--install`. This will add Tint to the prebuilt artifacts that are
available on GitHub, which some people would like.

commit.subject: Refactor DawnPerfTestWithParams SetUp
commit.message:
Refactor DawnPerfTestWithParams SetUp

DawnPerfTestWithParams::SetUp has a DAWN_TEST_UNSUPPORTED_IF
call inside which is supposed to skip the test. But, it was
called from dervied SetUp functions which would then continue
to run a bunch of setup code, even though all of that was
invalid and supposed to be skipped.

Refactored so DawnPerfTestWithParams has a SetUpPerfTest
virtual function that is only called if
DawnPerfTestWithParams::SetUp succeeds.

Change-Id: Iec1a5c23d5bf6cb6970a481c133c68266a6a6964

parents.subject: [dawn][native] Changes to DynamicArray updates to prep for resource updates

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Lazily initialize dynamic array resources
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Lazily initialize dynamic array resources

This CL sets up all the machinery to make BindGroup.Update() and friends
work and update the descriptors in the underlying VkDescriptorSets.
It tracks dirty resources in the DynamicArrayState and applies resource
updates in the Vulkan backend at the same time as the metadata buffer
updates.

The initialization code for dynamic array BindGroups is no longer needed
in the Vulkan backend as initial bindings are set using `Update`
internally, so InitializeDynamicBindings is turned into a function to
apply the ResourceUpdates instead.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: I8210add0198c2220e063b7fec7838f00011376ff

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Lazily initialize dynamic array resources
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Lazily initialize dynamic array resources

This CL sets up all the machinery to make BindGroup.Update() and friends
work and update the descriptors in the underlying VkDescriptorSets.
It tracks dirty resources in the DynamicArrayState and applies resource
updates in the Vulkan backend at the same time as the metadata buffer
updates.

The initialization code for dynamic array BindGroups is no longer needed
in the Vulkan backend as initial bindings are set using `Update`
internally, so InitializeDynamicBindings is turned into a function to
apply the ResourceUpdates instead.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: I8210add0198c2220e063b7fec7838f00011376ff

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Changes to DynamicArray updates to prep for resource updates
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Changes to DynamicArray updates to prep for resource updates

 - Include metadata for default bindings in the metadata buffer to make
   handling of default bindings consistent with user bindings. The only
   difference between the two is that the WGSL validation for
   hasResource/getResource checks against the user's size of the dynamic
   binding array.
 - Move the metadata buffer updates to be a member of a BindingUpdates
   struct that will also contain resource updates.

Change-Id: I1ca240c61732636e99ebda8c519f24c7596b701e

[spirv-reader] Handle spirv-opt deduplication.

The SPIR-V opt code will deduplicate aggregate structures with the same
shape. This means we can have two structs with different names and
different member names collapse to the same structure because the types
are the same.

This causes issues when going to WGSL as we end up losing one of the
structures. Instead, use the result_id as the type key when storing
converted types and don't use the spvtools Type when converting the
`Pointer`, `Array`, `RuntimeArray` or `Struct` types. Instead get the
inner element types directly from the SPIR-V instructions.

Bug: 347657112
Change-Id: I6dcb111a2c0b0822456a71d305836e584abfbec9

commit.subject: D3D12: Skip waiting on fences signaled by the same queue.
commit.message:
D3D12: Skip waiting on fences signaled by the same queue.

This avoids unnecessary waits on fences that were signaled by the same
internal queue. It also avoids re-creating a fence from a shared handle
if the fence is owned by Dawn's queue.

This optimization increases FPS by 1000 in the bug's sample WGPU test,
though it is still not enough to match WebGL's performance.

Bug: chromium:40066112
Change-Id: Ie635f6879eef769d68763b47a1306ec21b898d81

commit.subject: [ir] Validate vector construct element types
commit.message:
[ir] Validate vector construct element types

The intrinsics table lookup checks for overloads for both constructors
and conversions at the same time. When the construct instruction has a
mismatch between the argument element types and the result element
type, the intrinsic table lookup succeeds by finding the conversion
overload.

An IR `construct` instruction is not allowed to convert element types,
so add another check that the vector element types match.

Fixed: 464761429
Change-Id: Iba58287edf750f64938fcebba3b5e1361808cae6

feature that gathers both Snorm16TextureFormats and
Unorm16TextureFormats. Note that Norm16TextureFormats is not used
externally as well. The only feature used outside is
Unorm16TextureFormats.

commit.subject: [ir] Validate intermediate workgroup size products
commit.message:
[ir] Validate intermediate workgroup size products

When checking that the total workgroup size is less that UINT32_MAX,
we were only checking the final x*y*z product. This may overflow a
uint64_t and wrap around to be a valid uint32_t value, so we need to
check the intermediate products instead.

Fixed: 463283605
Change-Id: Ie4cb2354bc6693230b5b591d152ec3d95b0469c4

commit.subject: delete some preloaded libs on ubuntu-latest to prevent out of space error
commit.message:
delete some preloaded libs on ubuntu-latest to prevent out of space error

This, together with https://github.com/google/dawn/pull/51 allows the GitHub actions CI to complete all jobs, which has been failing since about November 14. This removes the preloaded dotnet, android and haskel libraries from the GitHub runner on Linux to reclaim enough space to finish building. I don't think any of these are relied on by dawn on Linux (and the build completes successfully), but someone should confirm that. The build happens is a container so I guess it is impossible it is relying on the host libraries anyway.

This is an imported pull request from
https://github.com/google/dawn/pull/52

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Implement BindGroup::InsertBinding
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Implement BindGroup::InsertBinding

 - Add a method to DynamicArrayState to return the first free slot (if
   any). It is O(n) for now but could be optimized to be O(logN) with a
   heap in the future.
 - Implement the bulk of InsertBinding using the method above and
   deferring the rest to Update().
 - Add tests for the behavior of InsertBinding.

Bug: 435317394

commit.subject: Kotlin: Prefix structures with GPU in addition to objects
commit.message:
Kotlin: Prefix structures with GPU in addition to objects

This change updates the Kotlin code generator to prefix all generated
WebGPU structure types (e.g., `DeviceDescriptor`) with "GPU".

The implementation involves:
* Modifying `dawn_json_generator.py` to add "GPU" to the class name when the entity category is 'structure'.
* Updating generator templates to use the prefixed naming logic for structure definitions and references.
* Updating the `BUILD.gn` file to reflect the new generated filenames (e.g. `AdapterInfo.kt` is now `GPUAdapterInfo.kt`).
* Updating existing Kotlin helper and test files to use the new class names.

commit.subject: Disable MSAA partial resolve for TransientAttachment usage
commit.message:
Disable MSAA partial resolve for TransientAttachment usage

Transient attachments cannot support partial resolve because their
contents are generally discarded or undefined at the start of a pass
(making the "load" part of a partial resolve impossible). This change
explicitly checks that `TransientAttachment` usage is NOT present.

Change-Id: I6b6642ff9c8efa575a297534eb22d5eb605511dc

commit.message:
Make Walk symlink-aware

Updates FSTestOSWrapper's Walk() to resolve any symlinks in the provided
path before performing any of the underlying logic. However, to be
consistent with Go's actual implementation, symlinks encountered while
walking are not followed. Tests that directly test behavior with
symlinks as well as _MatchesReal cases for symlinks are also added.

[dawn][utils] Add ScopedIgnoreValidationErrors

tracking on error objects: what matters is that the state tracking is
correct, not that the device produces validation errors for using the
error object.

CopyTextureToBufferCmd, and CopyTextureToTextureCmd structs to use
strong types (TexelOrigin3D and TexelExtent3D), and update code that

commit.subject: [spirv] Cleanup the SPIR-V writer options.
commit.message:
[spirv] Cleanup the SPIR-V writer options.

This CL splits apart the monolithic SPIR-V writer options and adds two
new structs.

The first, `Workarounds` contains any flags for polyfills we emit based
on specific drivers or conditions. These flags are all related to
working around issues in drivers.

commit.subject: GL: Add ExecuteSingleGLWork for unordered GL commands
commit.message:
GL: Add ExecuteSingleGLWork for unordered GL commands

Some GL commands, like resource creation, don't depend on prior
commands in the queue. Flushing the entire pending command list for
them is unnecessary.

This change introduces `Device::ExecuteSingleGLWork` to execute a
command immediately without a preceding flush. The existing work
execution function is renamed to `FlushPendingAndExecuteGLWork` to
clarify its flushing behavior.

This allows for more efficient execution of independent GL tasks.

Bug: 451928481
Change-Id: Ibc19ca6b2121fc5d511c59a0db010e7e8622646a

commit.subject: Change barrier usage tracking
commit.message:
Change barrier usage tracking

Stop tracking MapWrite/MapRead usage to issue HOST->GPU pipeline
barriers. Instead buffer will issue GPU->GPU barriers for all GPU
operations. We still eagerly transition buffers back to map usage, for
both mappable buffers and buffers used by Queue::WriteBuffer(), by
issuing a COMBINED_GPU->HOST barrier immediately before vkQueueSubmit().

Bug: 460180744
Change-Id: I4e6a7b1bd7ebd20b027ecdee26eae1c4e5764432

commit.subject: Vulkan: Only set configurations for `SubgroupSize` when it is used
commit.message:
Vulkan: Only set configurations for `SubgroupSize` when it is used

This patch skips all the configurations about `SubgroupSize`
(`VK_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE_BIT` and
`REQUIRED_SUBGROUP_SIZE_CREATE_INFO`) when the built-in variable
`subgroup_size` is not used in the current pipeline. On some platforms
the above configurations may cause performance loss when they are
actually not needed.

This patch also removes the toggle `VulkanDisallowVaryingSubgroupSize`
as it is no longer needed with this patch.

Bug: 410595996, 365910276
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: I65b520f3124e9c4344e60d1110138d0b20289ed3

commit.subject: Vulkan: Only use `ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE` when `SubgroupSizeControl` isn't enabled
commit.message:
Vulkan: Only use `ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE` when `SubgroupSizeControl` isn't enabled

This patch only use
`VK_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE_BIT`
when the Vulkan extension `SubgroupSizeControl` is not enabled
because according to Vulkan SPEC that flag cannot be set if a
`VkPipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfo` structure is
included in the pNext chain.

Bug: 410595996, 365910276
Change-Id: I65b520f3124e9c4344e60d1110138d0b20289ed3

commit.message:
Refine Color Format Setup

This commit revised Format.cpp according to this
comment(https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/247975/5/src/dawn/native/Format.cpp#584).

It refactors color format initialization into a two-phase process for
improved clarity. BuildFormatTable now defines the static properties of
each color format, while the new ConfigureColorFormatSupport function
dynamically assigns capabilities based on device features and
compatibility mode.

commit.subject: Add a tiled matrix multiply test to Dawn
commit.message:
Add a tiled matrix multiply test to Dawn

This is a more interesting test of subgroup matrix than existing
coverage.

It is also used to hit an issue with the Metal backend where the MSL
compiler produces a pipeline that has a maximum number of threads per
threadgroup that is lower than the workgroup size specified in the
WGSL shader.

Bug: 443794633
Change-Id: I8850cd1069901058cd763f121f0c9088486cde6e

commit.subject: Modify Buffer::MapAsync() validation
commit.message:
Modify Buffer::MapAsync() validation

Fix a bug where MapAsync callback can have success status when
MapAsyncImpl() threw an error and map operation actually failed.
BufferBaseTests.MapAsyncImplError is added to test this case. Also
ensure that |mState| is only loaded from once during APIMapAsync() to
avoid problems if the value changes on another thread.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add dynamic array mutator validation against GPU races
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add dynamic array mutator validation against GPU races

This CL adds the validation that prevents updating a binding while it
may still in use by the GPU.

 - Keep the pointer to the device in DynamicArrayState as it is used to
   query ExecutionSerials.
 - Add a `availableAfter` member to DynamicArrayState::BindingState
   following the logic in the bindless WebGPU proposal.
 - Allow passing an "empty" binding to DynamicArrayState::Update() that
   will mark the slot as used but not put anything in it.
 - Complete the implementation of BindGroup::Update / RemoveBinding that
   will call DynamicArrayState.
 - Add tests for all of the new validation. Some tests have to be
   end2end tests to make sure queue submission don't complete instantly.

Bug: 435317394
Change-Id: Ib0f66e69d0e4caac31cb0ce4e610a12941cd2756

trybots that are made available to Dawn. Chromium does not use any of
Dawn's Go code, so we can safely skip starting any builds for Go-only
changes.

commit.subject: Use dawn::SystemHandle class in more places.
commit.message:
Use dawn::SystemHandle class in more places.

Several tests do manual HANDLE management and contain leaks in error
codepaths.

To be able to use dawn::native::SystemHandle, we need to move it to
dawn::utils and switch the error handling away from the dawn::native
Error helpers to fail fast.

commit.subject: Use dawn::native::SystemHandle in end2end tests
commit.message:
Use dawn::native::SystemHandle in end2end tests

Multiple end2end tests do manual HANDLE management and have memory leaks
in error code paths.

To fix the leaks using RAII classes, dawn::native::SystemHandle must be
moved from dawn::native to dawn::util. Instead of SystemHandle relying
on the ResultOrError framework in dawn::native, SystemHandle will now
fails fast when duplicating and closing handles.

Fail fast code found double close bug in the GPUWriteThenCPURead test of
SharedTextureMemoryTests. Fixed that.

Change-Id: Ib4610b7b6db4df6da962693217d7bfbf97f337ef

commit.subject: tint/hlsl: Implement ArrayOffsetFromImmediates for dynamic buffer offsets
commit.message:
tint/hlsl: Implement ArrayOffsetFromImmediates for dynamic buffer offsets

This change enables HLSL backend to use immediate data blocks (root
constants) for storing dynamic storage buffer offsets, eliminating the
need for a separate uniform buffer when accessing buffers with dynamic
offsets.

Why:
- Reduces descriptor table usage in D3D12 by storing buffer offsets in
  root constants instead of requiring a dedicated uniform buffer
- Provides performance benefit by avoiding an extra buffer binding
- Brings HLSL backend to parity with buffer size optimization already
  implemented via ArrayLengthFromImmediates
- Enables D3D12 backend to migrate dynamic offset metadata to root
  constants (following CL 267454)

Components affected:
- ArrayOffsetFromUniformOptions: Added buffer_offsets_offset field to
  support immediate block storage at a specified offset
- PopulateBindingRelatedOptions: Updated to copy the new
  buffer_offsets_offset field from input options
- HLSL raise pipeline: Added buffer_offsets array creation in immediate
  data config, packed as array<vec4<u32>> for 16-byte alignment
- Transform selection: Conditionally uses ArrayOffsetFromImmediates
  when buffer_offsets_offset is set (runs BEFORE ChangeImmediateToUniform),
  otherwise falls back to ArrayOffsetFromUniform (runs AFTER)
- ArrayOffsetFromImmediates transform: New core IR transform that loads
  dynamic offsets from immediate blocks and adds them to all buffer
  access operations (Load/Store variants and Interlocked* atomics)
- Added 3 comprehensive tests: DynamicOffset_RobustnessAndDynamicOffsetFromImmediates,
  DynamicOffset_AtomicWithImmediates, DynamicOffset_MultipleBuffersWithImmediates

Bug: dawn:2428
Change-Id: I3c730cf5cd4bb196050c1fe43dc339ad51e1a186

tint/hlsl: Implement ArrayOffsetFromImmediates for dynamic buffer offsets

This change enables HLSL backend to use immediate data blocks (root
constants) for storing dynamic storage buffer offsets, eliminating the
need for a separate uniform buffer when accessing buffers with dynamic
offsets.

Reason:
- Reduces descriptor table usage in D3D12 by storing buffer offsets in
  root constants instead of requiring a dedicated uniform buffer
- Provides performance benefit by avoiding an extra buffer binding
- Brings HLSL backend to parity with buffer size optimization already
  implemented via ArrayLengthFromImmediates
- Enables D3D12 backend to migrate dynamic offset metadata to root
  constants (following CL 267454)

Components affected:
- ArrayOffsetFromUniformOptions: Added buffer_offsets_offset field to
  support immediate block storage at a specified offset
- PopulateBindingRelatedOptions: Updated to copy the new
  buffer_offsets_offset field from input options
- HLSL raise pipeline: Added buffer_offsets array creation in
  immediate data config, packed as array<vec4<u32>> for 16-byte
  alignment
- Transform selection: Conditionally uses ArrayOffsetFromImmediates
  when buffer_offsets_offset is set (runs BEFORE
  ChangeImmediateToUniform), otherwise falls back to
  ArrayOffsetFromUniform (runs AFTER)
- ArrayOffsetFromImmediates transform: New core IR transform that
  loads dynamic offsets from immediate blocks and adds them to all
  buffer access operations (Load/Store variants and Interlocked*
  atomics)

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: I3c730cf5cd4bb196050c1fe43dc339ad51e1a186
